page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.32xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz, it provides 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. The server configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor.

The hardware configuration is characterized by its high-capacity storage and network subsystems, integrating 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 133 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The bundled high-speed NVMe storage delivers low-latency local access for I/O-intensive operations without requiring separate network-attached storage for temporary data. The instance does not include GPU acceleration hardware and operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

By combining dense multithreaded compute, large memory capacity, bundled high-throughput local disk storage, and 133 Gbps networking, the instance reduces the need to provision separate network storage for data-heavy scratch tasks. These hardware characteristics make the instance suited for high-transaction relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, memory-intensive analytics, search index clusters, and large-scale enterprise application tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.32xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and equipped with an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz. It features 64 physical cores supporting 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core ratio. A key attribute of this configuration is its bundled storage subsystem, which delivers 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity to support low-latency high-throughput disk access directly on the host. The instance provides a 133 Gbps baseline network interface and includes no discrete GPU hardware. By coupling high-count compute with large-scale local NVMe disk and 133 Gbps networking, m8idb.32xlarge offers cost-efficient density for storage-heavy workloads without requiring dedicated external storage arrays. It is suited for enterprise relational databases, distributed caching layers, big data processing, and large transactional applications.
